knowledge.graph.title: Code graph
knowledge.graph.unknown: The code graph state is not available.
knowledge.graph.unknownHint: The CLI did not answer. Run the command in a terminal to see why.
knowledge.graph.offHint: It is off by default. When it is on, code lanes build a local map of the code for free and keep it current.
knowledge.graph.none: The graph is on, but no index exists yet. The next code lane builds it, or press the button.
knowledge.graph.behind: Changed since the index (added · changed · deleted)
knowledge.graph.density: Density (symbols per file · files with none)
knowledge.graph.thin: Most files hold no named symbol, so most questions asked of the graph will not find one. `orc graph audit` lists those files by language and says what their first declaration looks like.
knowledge.graph.drifted: Files changed after the last update. Lanes use the graph as hints only until it is updated. The update is free.
knowledge.graph.locator: The graph shows where code is and how it connects. Agents still read the code before they act on it.
knowledge.archive.note: Nothing is ever deleted here. Entries pushed out by the limit are moved, and they keep their id forever.
knowledge.archive.title: Archive
knowledge.blind.none: Nothing changed that no doc covers.
knowledge.blind.note: These files changed and no doc claims them. That is a gap in what is written down, not rot in what already exists — so it never makes the wiki stale on its own.
knowledge.blind.title: Changed, and no doc covers it
knowledge.coverage.naHint: It needs a registered wiki and a git repository.
knowledge.coverage.notATarget: This is a report, not a target. There is no threshold, nothing anywhere reacts to it, and a repo that deliberately writes about four subsystems out of forty is not broken.
knowledge.coverage.sub: {covered} of {tracked} tracked files are covered by at least one doc
knowledge.coverage.title: How much of the code is written about
knowledge.coverage.uncoveredNote: Grouped by folder and biggest first, because "240 files, all in vendor" and "12 files, all in payments" are opposite situations.
knowledge.debt.nothingBroken: Nothing is broken. These pages are behind, not wrong - and clearing the top of the list is far cheaper than a full re-scan.
knowledge.docs.field.title: Title
knowledge.docs.noneHint: Docs on disk have to be registered before anything can read them, and registering is free and instant.
knowledge.docs.note: Every registered doc, in the order the CLI returned them. Open a row to see what it covers and what it was scanned against. Each distance is measured against that doc's own files, so a doc about payments does not age because the README changed.
knowledge.docs.title: What is in the wiki
knowledge.field.distanceValue: {n} commits on the worst doc's covered files
knowledge.field.worst: Oldest doc (this is what sets the tier)
knowledge.gotchas.noneHint: A repair loop that goes red → green writes the first one.
knowledge.gotchas.note: One entry per project-specific failure a repair already solved. Pruning ARCHIVES the low-value tail — it never deletes.
knowledge.gotchas.pruneNone: Nothing would be archived — you are under the limit.
knowledge.gotchas.pruneWould: {n} entry(ies) would be moved to the archive:
knowledge.gotchas.title: Repair memory (gotchas)
knowledge.impact.blind: Structural blind spot — changed files no doc covers:
knowledge.impact.title: Refresh scope (orc wiki impact)
knowledge.one.lead: Update one doc, or add one topic, without re-planning a single other area. Both probes below are free and neither scans anything. The refresh or the add that follows is a lane, so it is a command to copy rather than a button.
knowledge.one.next: Run this in Claude Code. It costs model tokens, so nothing here starts it for you.
knowledge.one.placeholder: A topic, in your own words — "the remittance feature"
knowledge.one.proposed: A starting point, from path names only. Correct it before anything is scanned.
knowledge.one.title: One doc at a time
knowledge.orientation.missing: No orientation doc. Every reader opens it first, so this one is worth having — and regenerating it is free.
knowledge.orientation.present: Orientation doc present: {file}. Every reader opens it first.
knowledge.patterns.conflicts: Where the project and the playbook disagree
knowledge.patterns.literalNote: This exact text is put in front of every agent that writes code here. If you cannot read it, you cannot trust it.
knowledge.patterns.noneHint: Run /orc-pattern in Claude Code to codify one. Codifying costs a model, so this panel never does it.
knowledge.patterns.note: Reconciled per-language conventions, injected literally into executor slices. Project conventions win; security and correctness invariants are always kept.
knowledge.patterns.paidWhy: Learning a language's conventions reads a lot of your code, so it costs model tokens — a command to copy, not a button.
knowledge.patterns.title: Code patterns
knowledge.patterns.unheadered: This file has no readable header, so there is no date to show. A date is never guessed from when the file was last saved.
knowledge.peers.note: Linked repos, read-only. Every word here is what the other repo reported — this side never recalculates it. Editing the links happens on Crosslink; there is one picture of the boundary, and it lives there.
knowledge.peers.title: What ORC knows from next door
knowledge.plan.clean: Every page still covers the current code. Nothing to refresh.
knowledge.plan.freeFirst: Free repairs first - never pay for something a free step fixes
knowledge.plan.gone: A file this page documents is gone: {files}
knowledge.plan.naHint: Build a wiki first, or register the pages already on disk - both are free.
knowledge.plan.noEstimate: No cost estimate yet - there is not enough history to measure one, and none will be invented.
knowledge.plan.refreshWhy: A refresh re-reads your code with a model, so it costs money. That is why it is a command you run, not a button here.
knowledge.plan.retireHint: No run has used this page in the last {n}. Retiring it may be better value than refreshing it.
knowledge.plan.tierNote: Scan mode {mode}: {deep} deep, {light} light. A cheaper scan is always shown, never a quiet substitution.
knowledge.sub: What ORC already knows about this repo: the wiki, the code graph, cached code-patterns, and repair memory.
knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.usage.note: Counted from what runs actually put into a slice. A page nobody reads still costs money on every full refresh, and context room whenever it is included.
knowledge.wiki.freshNote: Freshness is coverage-relative: a doc is stale only when commits since its OWN anchor touched files IT covers.
knowledge.wiki.noneHint: Run /orc-wiki in Claude Code to build one. This panel never scans — that costs a model.
knowledge.wiki.syncHint: `orc wiki sync` fixes this instantly: registration is derived from the docs, so it is free and never a re-scan.
knowledge.wiki.unregistered: The wiki is {state} — nothing can read it until it is registered.
knowledge.graph.selfheal: It keeps itself current: a read repairs the files it is about to answer for, and the installed hook updates the map when a worker finishes. Nothing runs on a timer.
knowledge.gain.none: No graph reads recorded yet. The first `orc graph ctx` starts the ledger.
knowledge.gain.paid: Tokens put in (cards · source · hints · envelope)
knowledge.gain.hints: Hints (injected · read notes · updates · wide reads not hinted)
knowledge.gain.measure: Compare my ON and OFF runs
knowledge.gain.estimate: `avoided` is an estimate of the retrieval a read ladder would have paid for, never a bill. `paid` is exact.
knowledge.gain.measuredHead: {on} runs with the graph on vs {off} with it off
knowledge.gain.measuredFew: Too few runs to compare. Three runs in each group are needed; the rows are recorded and the comparison waits.
knowledge.gain.noise: a change smaller than the spread beside it is noise, not a result
knowledge.cg.exact.title: All the numbers, as the CLI sent them
knowledge.cg.exact.lead: The same numbers as the pictures above, with no drawing. Use this card when you need the exact value.
knowledge.cg.state.title: Where your code graph is now
knowledge.cg.state.lead: A code graph is always in one of four states. The lit box is the state of this repo now.
knowledge.cg.state.off: The feature is off. Nothing is built and nothing is read.
knowledge.cg.state.none: The feature is on, but the map is not built yet.
knowledge.cg.state.fresh: The map agrees with every file on disk. Lanes can trust it.
knowledge.cg.state.drifted: Some files changed after the last build. Lanes use the map as hints only.
knowledge.cg.state.loop: ↺ DRIFTED goes back to FRESH with one free update.
knowledge.cg.state.lineNote: This is the line a lane prints in the chat when it reads the graph:
knowledge.cg.now.off: To use the code graph, run this command in a terminal. Turning a feature on is your decision, so there is no button.
knowledge.cg.now.none: Build the map now. It is free: a parser reads the files, and no model runs.
knowledge.cg.now.drifted: Update the map now, or let the next lane do it. The update is free.
knowledge.cg.now.fresh: Nothing to do. The map is current.
knowledge.cg.flow.title: How the code graph works
knowledge.cg.flow.lead: The code graph is a local map of your code: where each function is, and what it connects to. It is made in five steps.
knowledge.cg.flow.codeWhat: The files that git tracks in this repo.
knowledge.cg.flow.parseWhat: Reads each file and finds functions, classes, routes, calls and imports.
knowledge.cg.flow.storeWhat: Kept on this machine, inside the ORC folder of this repo. Only changed files are read again.
knowledge.cg.flow.askWhat: A lane asks: where is this? Who calls it? What breaks if it changes?
knowledge.cg.flow.cardWhat: The agent gets a small answer with file:line. Then it reads only those lines.
knowledge.cg.flow.notes: Notes: a small model can write one sentence for each changed function. That is the only part that can cost a model. Notes mode here: {mode}.
knowledge.cg.anatomy.title: What a code graph looks like (an example, not your code)
knowledge.cg.anatomy.lead: Four small files from a made-up shop, drawn the way the graph sees them. Put the pointer on a dot to see what the graph knows about it.
knowledge.cg.anatomy.hint: Put the pointer on a dot, or move to it with the Tab key.
knowledge.cg.anatomy.route: A route. It uses requireAuth as middleware (a ref) and calls findOrder.
knowledge.cg.anatomy.list: A function. It calls findOrder. Nothing in the example calls it.
knowledge.cg.anatomy.auth: Middleware. The route refers to it by name, so a change here affects that route.
knowledge.cg.anatomy.find: Two symbols call it, and it calls query. A change here affects both callers.
knowledge.cg.anatomy.query: The end of the chain. A change here affects findOrder, and through it, two more symbols.
knowledge.cg.legend.fileWhat: One source file. The graph knows its path and which symbols are in it.
knowledge.cg.legend.symbolWhat: A named thing in a file: a function, a class, a method or a route.
knowledge.cg.legend.callWhat: One symbol calls another. The moving dot goes from the caller to the callee.
knowledge.cg.legend.refWhat: A symbol is given by name, for example as middleware or a callback.
knowledge.cg.num.title: Your graph, in numbers
knowledge.cg.num.symbolsWhat: Named things it found in those files.
knowledge.cg.num.perFileWhat: The average. A low value means most questions find nothing.
knowledge.cg.num.generationWhat: The build number. It goes up by one each time the map changes.
knowledge.cg.num.densityTitle: How many files hold a named symbol
knowledge.cg.num.densityNote: An empty file is not an error. It is a file where the parser found no named function or class, for example a template or a config file.
knowledge.cg.gain.title: What the graph cost, and what it probably saved
knowledge.cg.gain.noneHint: When a lane reads the graph, the cost and the estimate show here.
knowledge.cg.gain.lead: Both bars use the same scale. The top bar is what the graph put into agent context. The bottom bar is the searching it probably made unnecessary.
knowledge.cg.gain.range: the striped part is the range between the low and the high estimate
knowledge.cg.gain.readsTitle: Which questions lanes asked ({n} calls · {runs} runs)
knowledge.cg.read.ctx: Where a symbol is, who calls it, and what it calls.
knowledge.cg.read.forSlice: The outside view of each file in a task, before an executor starts.
knowledge.cg.read.impact: What else is affected if these files change.
knowledge.cg.read.map: The most connected files first. Used for planning.
knowledge.cg.read.changes: The symbols that the current diff touched, with a risk level.
knowledge.cg.read.cochange: Files that git history shows change together.
knowledge.cg.read.path: The chain of calls from one symbol to another.
knowledge.cg.gloss.title: What each word means
knowledge.cg.gloss.lead: Every word on this tab and in the exact card, in plain words.
knowledge.cg.gloss.file: A source file that git tracks. Very large files and generated folders are skipped.
knowledge.cg.gloss.symbol: A named function, class, method or route that the parser found.
knowledge.cg.gloss.call: A line from one symbol to another. The graph uses these lines to find callers and impact.
knowledge.cg.gloss.generation: The build number of the map. Each answer quotes it, so you can see which build an agent used.
knowledge.cg.gloss.freshDrifted: FRESH: the map agrees with the files. DRIFTED: some files changed since the build, so answers are hints and the code wins.
knowledge.cg.gloss.noneOff: NONE: the feature is on and no map exists yet. OFF: the feature is off.
knowledge.cg.gloss.behind: How many files were added, changed and deleted after the last build.
knowledge.cg.gloss.density: Symbols divided by files. A low value makes most questions come back empty.
knowledge.cg.gloss.thin: The CLI says THIN when most files hold no named symbol. `orc graph audit` shows which files, and why.
knowledge.cg.gloss.notes: The value of code_graph_notes. It sets when a small model writes one sentence for each changed function.
knowledge.cg.gloss.paid: The tokens the graph put into agent context. It is recorded, so it is exact.
knowledge.cg.gloss.envelope: The part of an answer that is not the card: labels, counts and the lines that lanes print.
knowledge.cg.gloss.avoided: The searching and file reading that the graph probably made unnecessary. It is an estimate, so it is always a range.
knowledge.cg.gloss.net: Avoided minus paid, in tokens and in tool calls. It is also a range.
knowledge.cg.gloss.hints: Short notes that the hook adds when an agent searches or reads a large file. They point to the graph.
knowledge.cg.gloss.measured: A button that compares your real runs with the graph on and off. It needs three runs in each group.
